observations: Opening establishes opposed wants immediately: Neet treats the appliance as an invader; Buddy checks both ends of the empty box for snacks. The second inspection provides a quiet physical joke before military escalation.

The repeated 30-degree mirroring and Heather being allowed through the blockade make Neet theatrical but purposeful. Sagar’s invader-tour narration differentiates his dry observer voice; Heather’s practical cleaner expectations remain distinct.

Buddy independently rides the machine, steals its brush, recoils from its dust collection, retrieves his sock and feels personally slighted when the robot prefers crumbs. The pause before “I showed it the bedroom” earns the reversal without explaining it.

Laundry confinement is causally clear: Neet diverts the robot, Buddy exits with the sock and shoulder-nudges the door, then the robot searches unsuccessfully. Morning illustration follows the explicit sock re-pickup, so the mouth-held prop is current.

The treaty follows mounting disruption and restores affectionate household cooperation. Reattached side brush answers Buddy’s lobbying; the human pause earns Neet’s upward glance. Buddy’s final snack-heist whisper carries his original desire into the warm ending.
Historical Tuesday treaty title remains after Thursday as explicitly recorded source choice; this reading does not resolve that chronology or infer owner-approved canon.
